trust.title: Trust this device
trust.intro: The box is its own certificate authority. Install its root certificate once on this device: the browser stops warning, reloads come from its cache, and you can sign in with a passkey.

windows.name: Windows:
windows.steps: Open the file, choose Install Certificate, Local Machine, then the store Trusted Root Certification Authorities.

macos.name: macOS:
macos.steps: Open the file in Keychain Access (keychain System), open the certificate and set Trust to Always Trust.

ios.name: iPhone and iPad:
ios.steps: Open the file in Safari and install the profile under Settings, General, VPN and Device Management, then switch it on under Settings, General, About, Certificate Trust Settings.

android.name: Android:
android.steps: Settings, Security, Encryption and credentials, Install a certificate, CA certificate, then pick the file.

linux.name: Linux:
linux.steps: Copy the file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run sudo update-ca-certificates; browsers with their own store need the step below.

firefox.name: Firefox:
firefox.steps: Settings, Privacy and Security, Certificates, View Certificates, Authorities, Import, and trust it to identify websites.

trust.restart: Afterwards restart the browser and open the box again by its name.
trust.untrusted: This device does not trust the box yet.
trust.unsupported: This connection cannot be checked: the box was opened over plain HTTP.
trust.hint: This device does not trust the box yet, so the browser warns and passkeys stay off.
trust.hintDismiss: Do not show again on this device

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: A passkey signs you in to the desktop without your password and second factor; your device asks for its PIN, fingerprint or face instead. SMB, SFTP, WebDAV and FTP keep using your password.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.nameHint: For example the device or the password manager it is kept in.
passkeys.removeConfirm: Remove the passkey {name}? It no longer signs you in.
passkeys.cancelled: The device did not create a passkey.

blocked.untrusted: Passkeys need a device that trusts the box.
blocked.address: Passkeys need the box opened by its name, not by an address, for example {url}.
blocked.browser: This browser does not support passkeys.
